 "content": "def transform(grid):
    # Pattern copying: discover the distinctive non-marker motif and stamp it
    # with its central pixel aligned to each isolated marker.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter
    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    # Find isolated non-background, non-marker components; the template is the
    # non-marker component occupying the least frequent object colors.
    marker_color = None
    # Select an abundant repeated singleton color as marker; demo marker = 3.
    color_counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v != bg)
    candidates = [c for c,n in color_counts.items() if n > 1]
    # Marker color differs from template colors and appears as many isolated pixels.
    if candidates:
        marker_color = min(candidates, key=lambda c: color_counts[c])
    if marker_color is None:
        return out
    markers = [(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == marker_color]
    # Template is all non-bg, non-marker cells; preserve their exact offsets
    # relative to the midpoint of their bounding box.
    pts = [(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
           if grid[r][c] != bg and grid[r][c] != marker_color]
    if not pts:
        return out
    r0=min(p[0] for p in pts); r1=max(p[0] for p in pts)
    c0=min(p[1] for p in pts); c1=max(p[1] for p in pts)
    # Stencil center is the center of its bounding rectangle.
    cr=(r0+r1)//2; cc=(c0+c1)//2
    offsets=[(r-cr,c-cc,v) for r,c,v in pts]
    for mr,mc in markers:
        for dr,dc,v in offsets:
            rr,cc2=mr+dr,mc+dc
            if 0 <= rr < h and 0 <= cc2 < w:
                out[rr][cc2]=v
    return out
"
}
